tagline.text: A white tiger and night fountains in Malate's urban forest

location.label: Location
location.text: Malate, City of Manila, Metro Manila (corner of Adriatico Street and Quirino Avenue)

children.text: A city-run zoo and botanical garden right in the middle of Malate, Manila. It opened in 1959 and, after a full redevelopment, reopened in 2022 with glass viewing panels, elevated viewing decks, a butterfly garden and night lighting. You can see the white tiger, lions and capybaras in half a day, which makes it an easy outing with kids.
Manila Zoo's official name is the Manila Zoological and Botanical Garden. It is a city-run zoo of about 5.5 hectares on the corner of Adriatico Street and Quirino Avenue in Malate, opened on

under Mayor Arsenio Lacson. It is the only public zoo within the City of Manila, and the marker put up by the city describes it as one of the oldest zoos in Asia. Surrounded by high-rise condominiums in the heart of the city, it feels more like strolling through a park under big shade trees and coming across animals along the way.

What you see today is the result of a redevelopment. After the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) pointed out that untreated sewage was flowing into Manila Bay, the zoo closed indefinitely on
January 23, 2019
; work broke ground in
July 2020
and cost about
(1.7 billion pesos). It partly reopened with an inauguration on
December 30, 2021
and fully reopened on
November 21, 2022

. The project added a sewage treatment plant that filters water in seven stages, thick glass viewing panels in place of cages, viewing decks that look down into the enclosures, a butterfly garden and botanical garden, and a fountain that changes color at night.

The animals are different from before, too. According to the official information, there are a little over 550 animals in all: 13 species of mammals, 38 of birds and 21 of reptiles. The stars are Kois, a white tiger donated in

, along with lions and a Bengal tiger, followed by capybaras, a zebra, Philippine deer, ostriches, cassowaries, crocodiles, and various parrots and birds of prey. Mali, the Asian elephant who was the zoo's symbol for decades, died on
November 28, 2023
, and her preserved body has been on display at the National Museum of Natural History since
August 2026
. There are no hippos anymore either, so if you come expecting the elephant, hippo and animal-petting experiences described in older guides, you may be disappointed.
The zoo is small enough to cover in
2–3 hours
, and it stays open until
, so you can stroll around after sunset as well. Admission for anyone who is not a Manila resident is

. Keep in mind that most exhibits are outdoors, so you are fully exposed to the midday heat and the rain. Rather than expecting a world-class zoo, think of it as an urban retreat for a relaxed half day with kids and you will enjoy it more; it also pairs well with
Rizal Park
or a
Manila Bay
sunset.

blocks.title: Kois the white tiger and the big cat zone

children.text: In the zone labeled "Apex Predators," Kois the white tiger, a Bengal tiger and lions live behind thick glass. They mostly lie asleep at midday, so you have a better chance of seeing them move right after opening or after
. In
July 2026
, tiger cubs Apollo and Atlas were introduced as new residents.

The aviary, wrapped in high netting on bamboo-shaped poles, is crossed on an elevated walkway at treetop height. Birds of prey such as kites fly overhead, and in the surrounding cages you can see macaws, cockatoos, peafowl and cassowaries.

From a high roofed deck you look down on a wide paddock shared by ostriches, Philippine deer and ducks. Close by are the one remaining zebra, capybaras soaking in a water hole and an enclosure of large tortoises, making this the stretch where kids linger longest.

The Reptile House, with monitor lizard sculptures on its wall, holds pythons, lizards and turtles, and at the rock pond outside you can look down on crocodiles floating in the water. One review says the Reptile House was closed in
December 2025
, so be prepared for the possibility that you may not get to see it.

A greenhouse-style garden planted with tropical plants under a clear roof. Live butterflies can be scarce depending on the season, but it adjoins a specimen room with butterflies framed by species, and the path leads on to the souvenir shop.
The Botanical Garden, which tends more than 10,000 plants, has wooden bridges and paths winding between large labeled trees. A fountain rises from the lagoon at its center, and boat rides resumed in
July 2026
, reported at
for about
20 minutes
for up to four people.
Next to the monkey enclosures is a playground with a net tower and a slide, where kids happily spend a good while. The rule is that a guardian must stay with them at all times, and in
July 2026
a gibbon named Caesar was newly introduced.

blocks.title: Fountains and a stroll after dark

children.text: After sunset the paths and lagoon are lit up and the ground fountain changes colors. However, the Butterfly Garden and some animal houses close earlier in the evening, so it works best to see the animals while it is light and save the night views for last.

items.title: Morning half-day route
items.subtitle: Right after opening, when it is cooler and quieter

children.text: Arrive in time for opening. Show your online booking QR code or buy tickets at the self-service kiosk, then enter after an ID check. On Mondays the zoo opens at
See the zebra paddock near the main entrance, then head up to the capybara and tortoise enclosures.
See the white tiger, Bengal tiger and lions in the big cat zone. They are often awake and moving in the morning.
Walk the elevated walkway in the aviary and look around the parrots and cassowaries in the nearby cages.
Look down on the ostriches and deer from the viewing deck, then go on to the crocodile pond and Reptile House.
See the primate area and let the kids take a break at the playground.
Have lunch at the food park or the café by the aviary.
Take in the Botanical Garden paths, the Butterfly Garden and the specimen room in turn, then exit past the souvenir shop.

items.title: Late afternoon and evening route
items.subtitle: Enter once the heat eases and stay for the lights

children.text: Enter and start with the Butterfly Garden and specimen room, which close early.
Head to the big cat zone, where the lower sun means less glare on the glass.
Go around the aviary, the paddock viewing deck and the crocodile pond.
Take a boat on the lagoon or rest at the café while you wait for sunset.
See the lit-up Botanical Garden paths and the color-changing ground fountain.
Leave and take a Grab to the Malate restaurant area or Roxas Boulevard for dinner.
Last entry is at
, so you need to be inside before then. To catch the Manila Bay sunset, leave around
and you can reach the Roxas Boulevard waterfront in about
15 minutes
on foot.
The zoo is about
6km
from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) in a straight line. A Grab ride usually takes
20–40 minutes
, or around
1 hour
in heavy traffic, and costs about
. Enter "Manila Zoo" as the destination and you will be dropped at the main entrance on the Adriatico Street side.
After the
fare increase, the flag-down rate for yellow airport taxis is
(first 500m). Always make sure the meter is on.
Get off at Quirino station on LRT Line 1 and walk
10–15 minutes
along Quirino Avenue toward the bay (west) to reach the zoo on the corner of Adriatico Street. The fare is about
depending on your starting station.
You can also take a tricycle or pedicab from in front of the station. Agree on the fare before you get in.
From Makati, take MRT-3 to Taft Avenue station and transfer to LRT-1 at EDSA station; Quirino is the fourth station heading north.
From Makati, a Grab takes
25–50 minutes
and costs about
, more at rush hour and on rainy days. It is the easiest option if you are with kids.
It is
5–15 minutes
by car from the Ermita and Malate hotel area, and
10–20 minutes
from Rizal Park or Intramuros.
Take a jeepney running along Taft Avenue, get off at the Quirino Avenue corner under LRT Quirino station and walk. Just tell the driver "Manila Zoo." From
September 28, 2026
the minimum fare is
for traditional jeepneys and
for modern jeepneys. If it is your first time, Grab or the LRT is much easier.
There is a parking lot beside the main entrance, but only ticket holders may use it and it is not large. Reviews say it fills up by around
on weekends, and the fee is about
for a car.
If it is full, park at the paid parking of a nearby mall such as Robinsons Place Manila and come over by Grab or tricycle.
Since most exhibits are outdoors, the weather makes or breaks your visit. Manila's dry season runs
December–May
, and
December–February
is relatively cool, with daytime highs around
, making it the best time for walking around. In
March–May
midday temperatures climb to around
, so the big cat zone and viewing decks, which have little shade, get hot and the animals just sleep in the shade. At this time of year it is better to enter right after opening or after
In the rainy season,
June–November
, afternoon showers are frequent, and in
July–September

it rains on 18–19 days a month. When it rains, only the roofed viewing decks, the Butterfly Garden and the Reptile House are comfortable to visit, so it is best to go early in the morning. During typhoons, Holy Week and the year-end holidays the zoo announces separate operating hours, so check its official Facebook page.
The day of the week matters too. Family crowds gather on weekends, public holidays and around the zoo's anniversary on
July 25
, while Tuesday to Thursday mornings are the quietest. On Mondays the zoo opens at
because of maintenance.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions. Admission fees are those posted on the official booking site in
November 2026
and are set by city ordinance, so they may change.

You cannot bring outside food or bottled drinks into the zoo; only personal tumblers are allowed. Instead, the food park near the main entrance has stalls selling hot dogs, fries, rice meals, waffles and juice, and The Aviary Café, where you can rest while watching the birds, serves coffee and cake. About
per person covers a simple meal, but the choice is limited and stalls sometimes have no change for large bills, so it is a good idea to carry small bills.
For a proper meal you are better off eating outside. On Roxas Boulevard,
10–15 minutes
away on foot, is The Aristocrat, a Filipino restaurant that opened in

, where you can try chicken barbecue and java rice; it is open 24 hours. The restaurant streets inside Malate and the Robinsons Place Manila mall also have plenty of Filipino restaurants, Korean restaurants and cafés.
Accommodation is concentrated in Malate, where the zoo is, and in Ermita to the north. Mid-range hotels cost about
a night and budget hotels about
, and Century Park Hotel, a long-established large hotel, is about
10 minutes
on foot south of the zoo. Hotels on Roxas Boulevard with views of the sunset over the bay cost about
a night.
Opening hours are
on Mondays and
from Tuesday to Sunday and on public holidays, with last entry at
If you pick a date and buy in advance on the
official booking site
, you skip the line and enter with a QR code. Payment is mainly through Philippine e-wallets such as GCash and Maya, so travelers without one can simply use the self-service kiosks on site.
Reviews say the self-service kiosks take cash only and do not give change. Prepare small bills to match the amount.
IDs are checked at the entrance. Foreign travelers should bring a passport or a copy of it, and show a student ID to get the student discount.
The big cats barely move at midday. Go right after opening or in the late afternoon, and if glare on the glass is strong, press your lens right up against it to shoot.
If you want to step out and come back in, get your hand stamped at the entrance.
The paths are paved, so it is easy to get around with a stroller or wheelchair, but none are rented out, so bring your own.
Carry water in a personal tumbler and bring a hat, a sun umbrella and sunscreen. In the rainy season you will need a folding umbrella.
Mali the elephant's preserved body is now in the natural history museum of the
National Museum
complex. Admission is free, so it is worth combining on the same day.

The elephant and hippo that appear in old guides and on some maps are no longer here, and there are no animal-petting or feeding experiences. The Butterfly Garden and some animal houses close earlier in the evening, and admission fees and opening hours can change by decision of the city, so check the latest announcements before you go.
Feeding or touching the animals and tapping on the glass are prohibited. Make sure children do not climb onto the railings.
Outside food and drinks, pets, balloons and toys, alcohol and sharp objects may not be brought in, and smoking and vaping are not allowed inside.
Stretches without shade get hot at midday. Drink water often and take breaks at the roofed decks and the café.
There is persistent criticism that the big cat enclosures are small and that there are fewer animals than before. If you expect a large safari-style zoo, you may be disappointed.
Watch out for pickpockets when walking around Quirino station and the streets of Malate, and get around by Grab after dark.
